purpose: Primary Fair Work Commission case ledger preserving job-search effort, alternative employment, an explicit non-return decision attributed to a workplace mechanism, and an ordered compensation remedy without treating the order as payment receipt.

events.geography: Melbourne, Australia; Fair Work Commission case [2023] FWC 2485
events.date_precision: dismissal date; decision records new employment on 2023-09-04 and compensation order within 21 days
events.denominator: One publicly identified adjudicated worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision and linked order reference
events.missingness: Worker identity beyond the public case name, alternative-offer set, payment receipt, net household effect, later job duration, recurrence, collective action, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: The employer dismissed a part-time sales/beauty consultant after disputed performance warnings and an unresolved customer-allocation or sales-target mechanism
events.alternatives_before_action: The worker applied for 11 job vacancies between 2023-07-07 and 2023-08-14 and began new full-time employment on 2023-09-04; the public record does not enumerate other feasible offers or non-use choices
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The worker was out of work for seven weeks and five days; the Commission found the new role paid at least an equivalent amount and assessed economic loss at $4,312
events.choice_or_response: The worker challenged the warnings, sought clarification and assistance, filed an unfair-dismissal application, applied for alternative jobs, and stated she no longer wished to return because of the employer's customer-allocation mechanism
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employer controlled warnings, customer allocation, and termination; the worker controlled challenge, job search, and non-return position; the Commission controlled remedy
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission found dismissal unfair, deemed reinstatement inappropriate, and ordered $4,312 compensation within 21 days
events.durability_followup: New employment and refusal of reinstatement are observed; payment, job duration, recurrence, and household recovery remain unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Alternative employment, explicit non-return reasoning, assessed economic loss, and an ordered compensation remedy are observed; payment receipt is not
events.protected_outcome: The worker obtained a new role and a formal compensation route; the Commission found no economic loss after the new employment began
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker lost seven weeks and five days of work and the original employment relationship; customer-allocation concerns and the longer-term employment effect remain bounded
events.cost_risk_transfer: The worker carried search and unemployment costs before the new role; the employer was assigned a compensation obligation subject to execution
events.later_outcome: New employment and a stated refusal of reinstatement are observed, but payment receipt, job duration, household recovery, recurrence, later trust, collective action, switching, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The worker's stated non-return position attributes an unacceptable employment relationship to the customer-allocation mechanism; this is a case-level meaning/action signal, not a standardized trust measure
events.public_or_collective_response: The worker used the formal Commission route and job-search response; no later collective or political action is reported
events.counterexample: Alternative employment and non-return can coexist with economic loss and a compensation order; an explicit refusal to return is not the same as measured institutional distrust or practical exit
events.source_and_uncertainty: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2023] FWC 2485, https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2023fwc2485.pdf; decision records 11 applications, new employment, non-return reasoning, assessed loss, and a 21-day compensation order, but no payment receipt or later follow-up

arrows.evidence: The decision records 11 job applications from July 7 to August 14 and new full-time employment beginning September 4 after dismissal on June 28
arrows.counterexample: Job-search counts and a new role do not reveal all available alternatives, search costs, or whether the new job was equivalent
arrows.remaining_gap: Offer set, search intensity, constraints, job duration, and long-term equivalence

arrows.evidence: The worker submitted that reinstatement was inappropriate because she no longer wished to work there due to the customer-allocation mechanism; the Commission observed alternative employment
arrows.counterexample: A stated non-return reason is not a standardized trust scale or proof that all future platform/workplace options were rejected
arrows.remaining_gap: Meaning intensity, trust, identity, later switching, and whether non-return was voluntary under feasible alternatives

arrows.from: alternative employment and assessed seven-week loss
arrows.evidence: The Commission found economic loss of $4,312 and ordered compensation in that amount within 21 days
arrows.counterexample: An order and deadline do not prove payment receipt or net recovery
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment execution, receipt, taxation, and residual loss

arrows.to: later trust, recovery, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public decision ends at the new role, non-return reasoning, and compensation order without later household, trust, recurrence, or exit follow-up
arrows.counterexample: A non-return decision may reflect a bounded workplace dispute rather than durable institutional distrust or broad labor-market exit
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment receipt, job duration, household recovery, later trust, recurrence, collective action, switching, and exit

arrows.evidence: The Commission found the dismissal unfair and ordered compensation, but the public decision reports no employer correction to the customer-allocation mechanism or recurrence monitoring
arrows.counterexample: Individual compensation can coexist with unchanged workplace allocation practices
arrows.remaining_gap: Process correction, recurrence, worker voice, monitoring, and comparable-worker outcomes

boundary: This ledger adds one primary adjudicated case with observed job-search effort, alternative employment, an explicit non-return decision tied to a workplace mechanism, and an ordered compensation remedy. It does not establish payment receipt, full trust measurement, household recovery, recurrence, action, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, direct identifier beyond the public case reference, bulk archive, or payment instrument is retained; only bounded primary decision fields, dates, observed job-search and non-return stages, remedy amount, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
